scenarios.title: Flooded Road Ahead
scenarios.description: You're driving home and the road ahead is covered in fast-moving water. It doesn't look too deep from here.

choices.text: Drive through slowly, staying in the middle of the road
choices.feedback: Just a foot of moving water can sweep a car away, and depth is hard to judge from the driver's seat. The safest rule is: Turn Around, Don't Drown.

choices.text: Turn around and find another route
choices.feedback: Correct. Never drive through floodwater, even if it looks shallow. Roads can be washed out underneath, and cars can stall or float away in seconds.

choices.text: Get out and check the water depth on foot first
choices.feedback: Walking into moving floodwater is just as risky as driving through it. A few inches can knock an adult off their feet. Avoid entering it entirely.

scenarios.title: Rising Water at Home
scenarios.description: Heavy rain has caused water to start entering the ground floor of your house. It's rising steadily.

choices.text: Go down to the basement to check on your belongings
choices.feedback: Basements fill first and fastest during a flood, and exits can be cut off. Never head toward low ground once water is entering the building.

choices.text: Move to the highest floor and turn off utilities if it's safe to do so
choices.feedback: Correct. Getting to higher ground protects you from rising water, and switching off gas and electricity (if safely reachable) reduces fire and shock risks.

choices.text: Stay on the ground floor and wait to see if the water stops rising
choices.feedback: Waiting on a floor that's already flooding wastes time you may need to reach safety. Move to higher ground as soon as water starts entering the home.

scenarios.title: Downed Power Line Near Water
scenarios.description: You're evacuating on foot and notice a fallen power line lying partly in a pool of standing water ahead.

choices.text: Walk around it, staying as far from the water as possible
choices.feedback: Correct. Standing water near downed lines can be electrified. Keeping a wide distance from both the line and any water it touches is the safest choice.

choices.text: Step carefully through the shallow edge of the water to pass quickly
choices.feedback: Water in contact with a downed power line can carry a lethal electric current. Never touch or walk through water near fallen lines, no matter how shallow.

choices.text: Move the power line out of the way with a nearby stick
choices.feedback: Power lines can carry a lethal charge even through objects like sticks. Never touch a downed line directly or indirectly. Keep your distance and report it.

scenarios.title: Evacuation Order
scenarios.description: Authorities warn that a river is about to overflow and tell your neighbourhood to evacuate. The water has not reached your street yet.

choices.text: Wait until the water reaches your street before deciding
choices.feedback: Floodwater can rise very quickly and cut off roads. Leave while the route is still safe.

choices.text: Leave now with essentials and follow the official route to higher ground
choices.feedback: Correct. Evacuate early, take only what you need, and use the routes authorities recommend.

choices.text: Stay home and move the car into the garage
choices.feedback: A garage will not protect a car or you from a serious flood, and delaying risks being trapped.

scenarios.title: Car in Rising Water
scenarios.description: Water is rising around your car on a low road and the engine has stalled. The water is not yet above the doors.

choices.text: Stay inside and wait for it to pass
choices.feedback: Rising water can lift a car and sweep it away. Waiting inside can trap you.

choices.text: Get out now and move to higher ground on foot if it is safe to do so
choices.feedback: Correct. Leave the vehicle early while you still can, and head for higher ground. Cars are replaceable, people are not.

choices.text: Try to restart the engine and drive through
choices.feedback: Driving through floodwater is dangerous. Even shallow water can stall a car or carry it away.

scenarios.title: After the Water Goes Down
scenarios.description: The flood is receding. A neighbour wants to wade through the water in the street to start cleaning up.

choices.text: Wade through barefoot, since the water looks clear
choices.feedback: Floodwater can carry sewage, chemicals and sharp objects even when it looks clean, and it can hide holes and live wires.

choices.text: Avoid it if possible, and if you must go in, wear waterproof boots and gloves and wash well afterwards
choices.feedback: Correct. Floodwater is often contaminated. Protect your skin, wash up, and wait for confirmation before drinking tap water.

choices.text: Drink the tap water to stay hydrated while you work
choices.feedback: Tap water may be contaminated after a flood. Use bottled water until officials say it is safe.
